clue.text: Pretentiousness, a poet displaying facial growth

parts.note: side is an old informal word for putting on airs or swank
Robert Burns, the Scottish poet

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at an affected poet showing off his whiskers.
explanation.definitionFit: Sideburns are strips of whiskers grown down the cheeks, a kind of facial hair.

clue.text: Neat appearance of vehicles going up to the loch

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the word for vehicles is read from bottom to top

parts.note: trams are street vehicles running on rails
Loch Ness, the best-known Scottish loch

explanation.surface: Some tidy-looking vehicles drive up the road towards a Scottish lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Being well turned out and tidy is the quality of looking smart.

clue.text: Curtain protecting old flag

indicators.note: the curtain word wraps around the letter for old, as if shielding it

parts.note: a drop is a theatre curtain lowered onto the stage

explanation.surface: A curtain is hung to shelter an ancient banner.
explanation.definitionFit: To flag is to tire or sag, which is to wilt or hang limply.

clue.text: Black reptile crossing zoo's entrance in violent snowstorm

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

indicators.note: the reptile word straddles the extra letter, crossing over it on both sides

parts.note: a lizard is a scaly reptile

indicators.note: the entrance of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A dark reptile wanders across the zoo gate during a fierce blizzard-like storm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'zoo's entrance' gives Z, which goes inside LIZARD to make LIZZARD, after B.
explanation.definitionFit: A blizzard is a severe storm of driving snow and strong wind.

clue.text: Drinking its contents would get a tramp into the papers!

definitions.text: Drinking its contents would get a tramp into the papers!

indicators.note: the vagrant word is put inside the word for papers

parts.note: a ream is a quantity of paper, 500 sheets
a hobo is an American tramp or vagrant

explanation.surface: Downing a huge bottle of wine would land a vagrant in the newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a giant bottle of wine whose contents could make anyone a drunken headline.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehoboam is an outsized wine or champagne bottle holding six standard bottles, enough to get anyone drunk.

clue.text: Trim a tree

definitions.meaning: trim as an adjective means neat and smart in appearance
a coniferous evergreen tree of the pine family

explanation.definitionFit: Spruce means neat and smart as an adjective, and is also the name of a common conifer.

clue.text: Loose leaves cause many to abandon cricket, perhaps

indicators.note: the letter for many walks out of the word for cricket, leaving it behind

parts.note: a cricket is an example of an insect
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so stands for many

explanation.surface: Falling leaves force a crowd to give up the cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cricket' looks like the British bat-and-ball game, but it is the chirping bug, an INSECT; removing C leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An inset is a set of extra pages slipped into a magazine or book, so separate unbound sheets.

clue.text: Notoriety among soccer administrators? Goodness!

parts.note: in means among or amid
the FA is the Football Association, which runs English football
my! is an exclamation of surprise, like goodness!

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at the bad reputation of football's governing body.
explanation.definitionFit: Infamy is a bad reputation, the state of being well known for something wicked.

clue.text: Looking endlessly around university for a marine biologists's specimen

indicators.note: the shortened searching word goes around the letter for university
endlessly means the last letter is cut off the word

parts.note: searching means looking for something

explanation.surface: Academics hunt everywhere around campus for a sea creature to study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts the final G from SEARCHING to give SEARCHIN, and U goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea urchin is a spiny sea creature, the sort of specimen collected by those who study ocean life.

clue.text: Not up to a student to write such music

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written before being turned round
L is for learner, from the L-plates on a learner driver's car

explanation.surface: A music student is told they are not capable of composing this.
explanation.walkthrough: 'such music' needs the clue's opening to work as a description: music in a key, which a student is told they can write.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonal music is written in a key, organised around a home note, as opposed to atonal music.

clue.text: Do away with a round lake in error

indicators.note: the letters for round and lake are placed inside the slang word for a mistake

parts.note: bish is British slang for a blunder or mistake
O is round in shape
L is a standard abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: Someone mistakenly wants to get rid of a circular lake.
explanation.walkthrough: BISH is old British slang for a mistake; O and L go inside it after A.
explanation.definitionFit: To abolish is to formally end or scrap something, such as a law.

clue.text: Judge found bad weather a burden

parts.note: a referee, ref, judges a sports match
rain is a type of bad weather

explanation.surface: A referee finds the wet weather heavy going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'burden' looks like a load, but it is the old word for the chorus of a song.
explanation.definitionFit: A burden in music is a chorus repeated after each verse of a song.

clue.text: Mineral conveyed to a Bolivian city, not an American one

parts.note: to is the direction of conveying, taken as the word to itself

indicators.note: not means the American city is to be taken out of the Bolivian one

parts.note: La Paz is the seat of government of Bolivia
LA is Los Angeles, a US city

explanation.surface: A gemstone is shipped to South America rather than the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'an American one' is the US city of Los Angeles, which is taken out of the Bolivian city's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Topaz is a silicate gemstone, often yellow, found as a crystal.

clue.text: Like Westminster Parliament's 75% charge for housing TV equipment

indicators.note: the shortened charge word holds the equipment word inside it
75% means three of the four letters of the charge word are kept

parts.note: a bill is a charge for goods or services
a camera is the equipment used to film television

explanation.surface: Parliament's spending on cameras for broadcasting is criticised.
explanation.walkthrough: '75%' keeps three of the four letters of BILL, so BIL, which holds CAMERA.
explanation.definitionFit: Bicameral means having two chambers, as the UK Parliament has the Commons and the Lords.

clue.text: Many peer awkwardly, discerning the highest heaven

indicators.note: awkwardly means these letters are clumsily shuffled into a new order

explanation.surface: A crowd of lords squint clumsily, trying to make out paradise.
explanation.definitionFit: The empyrean is the topmost sphere of heaven in ancient cosmology, the sky or paradise.

clue.text: Collecting hobby of Greek character in recent times

parts.note: phi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
lately means recently

explanation.surface: A Greek has taken up a pastime only recently.
explanation.definitionFit: Philately is stamp collecting, a pastime of gathering postage stamps.

clue.text: One dismissed by the head cook

indicators.note: the letter for one is sent away from the word for head

parts.note: a chief is the head of a group
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A worker is sacked by the head chef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head cook' reads as one phrase; 'head' belongs to the wordplay and 'cook' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A chef is a professional cook, especially one running a kitchen.

clue.text: Fine gold obtained in America left behind by mistake

parts.note: F is an abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads
or is the heraldic term for gold
gotten is the American past participle of get

explanation.surface: Fine gold acquired in the US was accidentally left behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Something forgotten has slipped from memory and been unintentionally left somewhere.

clue.text: It may help propel sick animals round island

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go round the letter for island
sick means the letters are disordered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Something that keeps ailing beasts moving circles an island.
explanation.definitionFit: The mainsail is a ship's principal sail, catching the wind to drive the vessel forward.

clue.text: In which some are bent on supporting the vaults

definitions.text: In which some are bent on supporting the vaults

parts.words: In which some are bent on supporting the vaults
parts.note: sounds like church cellars, but describes a playground game where crouching players are jumped over

explanation.surface: Some people are dedicated to holding up a church's underground arches.
explanation.definitionFit: Leapfrog is a children's game in which players bend over while others vault over their backs.

clue.text: Previously mentioned, this port

definitions.meaning: ... as in the aforesaid, already referred to
Port ..., the Egyptian port at the Suez Canal

explanation.definitionFit: Said means aforementioned in legal phrasing, and Port Said is an Egyptian harbour city at the canal's mouth.

clue.text: Mine host is a frequenter of Lords

definitions.meaning: mine host is an old jocular term for an innkeeper
the Lord's ... are a cricket charity linked with Lord's, the London cricket ground

explanation.definitionFit: A taverner keeps an inn, and the Lord's Taverners are a charity of cricket-lovers named after Lord's, London's famous cricket ground.

clue.text: Leafy glade, not initially a place of refuge

indicators.note: the first letter of the refuge word is dropped

parts.note: a harbour is a place of shelter, especially for ships

explanation.surface: A shady clearing is not, at first, considered a safe haven.
explanation.definitionFit: An arbour is a shady garden retreat formed by trees or climbing plants.

clue.text: Dirty mark in house is mud, generally

indicators.note: in means the letters run inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A grubby stain in the home is usually caused by mud.
explanation.definitionFit: A smudge is a blurred smear of dirt.

clue.text: Stone extractor employed as river transport worker

parts.note: qua is Latin for in the capacity of, meaning as
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a means of transport
man means a worker or employee, as in man the pumps

explanation.surface: A man who cuts stone has taken a job on river boats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'river transport worker' reads as a ferryman, but splits into three short pieces; 'employed' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarryman works in a quarry, cutting and extracting stone.

clue.text: Question mark about a student's sudden sickness

indicators.note: the question and mark letters wrap around the following letters

parts.note: M is an abbreviation for mark, the old German currency
L is for learner, from L-plates

explanation.surface: A query over a student's marks causes nausea.
explanation.definitionFit: A qualm is a sudden feeling of nausea, as well as a pang of doubt.

clue.text: Courtyard laid out by Irishman originally in Omagh

parts.note: Pat is a typical Irish man's name

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A yard designed by an Irishman first built in Omagh, a town in Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A patio is a paved outdoor area beside a house, like a small courtyard.

clue.text: Silent bird without a note

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the bird surrounds the letters

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird
C is a musical note

explanation.surface: A songbird is quiet, without a single note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' seems to mean lacking, but here means outside: TIT goes round A and C.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacit means unspoken or implied without words.

clue.text: Help to protect an emperor's barometer

indicators.note: the help word surrounds the emperor's name as if shielding him

parts.note: aid means help
Nero was a Roman emperor

explanation.surface: Assistance is sent to guard an emperor's weather instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: An aneroid is a barometer that measures air pressure without using liquid.

clue.text: A small loop of thread containing right colour

indicators.note: the loop word holds the letter for right inside it

parts.note: a picot is a small decorative loop of thread on lace edging

explanation.surface: A tiny loop of yarn holds the correct shade.
explanation.definitionFit: Apricot is a pale orange-yellow shade, named after the fruit.

clue.text: Horse, say, for the council leader

indicators.note: say signals a word that sounds like another when spoken

parts.note: a mare is a female horse

explanation.surface: A horse, for instance, has been chosen to lead the town council.
explanation.definitionFit: A mayor is the elected head of a town or city council.

clue.text: Inform bridge opponents twice about this solution

indicators.note: the doubled bridge players go about the crossword word
twice means the bridge pair is written two times

parts.note: in bridge, East and North sit at adjacent seats and are opponents
a light is a crossword answer entered in the grid

explanation.surface: Teach card players twice about how this puzzle works.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, players are named by compass points and partners sit opposite, so East and North are opponents; 'this solution' is a light, the crossword's own word for an answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlighten someone is to give them knowledge or understanding.
